basis: Fanconi tubular dysfunction and ichthyosis define the syndrome; jaundice and diarrhea alone do not establish direct hepatic or intestinal damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: jaundice is reported, but its mechanism and associated hepatic injury are not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea alone does not establish persistent intestinal injury or loss of function.

basis: Umbrella of organic acid metabolism disorders; lasting neurologic injury varies substantially by subtype and is not established in >=30% across the group.

decisions.neurologic: none: some subtypes cause frequent brain injury, but others usually preserve development; >=30% lasting neurologic involvement across this umbrella is not established.

basis: Defining hepatic glycogen storage; renal storage dysfunction affects >30% over time; supplied HPO reports cognitive impairment in 80-99%. Immune defects chiefly concern subtype Ib.

decisions.neurologic: involved: supplied HPO explicitly reports cognitive impairment in 80-99%, supporting persistent neurologic dysfunction rather than hypoglycemic seizures alone.

basis: Complement-mediated microangiopathy defines renal injury, hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; secondary hypertension does not establish additional direct cardiovascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension occurs in 30-79% but is secondary to renal disease and separately diagnosable; common additional direct cardiovascular injury is not established.

basis: M. xenopi disease predominantly presents as chronic destructive pulmonary infection; extrapulmonary sites are uncommon.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the lungs are the predominant site occupied and damaged by clinical M. xenopi infection, rather than a downstream complication.

basis: Intestinal motility dysfunction defines the disease; cataract occurs in 1/2 reported patients. Pes valgus and hypotonia do not establish additional tissue damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes valgus in 1/2 describes foot alignment without established functional damage; hypotonia alone does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.

basis: Craniofacial/limb dysplasia and cardiac defects define syndrome; ptosis occurs in 30-79%, pulmonary hypoplasia in 1/2. Small denominators limit certainty.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: structural cardiac defects are explicitly part of the syndrome definition; ventricular septal defect is reported in 2/2 assessed patients.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is direct developmental loss of lung tissue, reported in 1/2 patients; supplied frequency exceeds 30%, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining early neurodegeneration; hepatic storage with cholestatic injury affects roughly >=30% of severe infantile cases. Splenic enlargement alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic storage and enlargement are common, but functional splenic impairment or blood-cell damage in >=30% is not established.

basis: Hereditary glycinergic startle disorder; supplied ancestry explicitly includes neurotransmitter-deficiency metabolic disease. Apnea in 1/6 does not support pulmonary involvement.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the supplied ancestry identifies a neurotransmitter-deficiency metabolic disorder, consistent with defective glycine transport and recycling.

basis: Severe skeletal dysplasia with rib fractures in 20/20; pulmonary and structural CNS abnormalities lack established >=30% frequencies or clear major diagnostic status.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia is reported without frequency; thoracic hypoplasia and lethality alone do not establish direct lung involvement in >=30%.
decisions.neurologic: none: cerebellar hypoplasia and ventriculomegaly are reported without frequencies; >=30% direct CNS involvement or major diagnostic status is not established.
